text: In twenty thirty-eight, some computers will think it's nineteen-oh-one.
They count time in seconds since January first, nineteen seventy.
And many store that count in a signed thirty-two-bit number.
Its limit: about two point one billion seconds.
That runs out on January nineteenth, twenty thirty-eight.
One second later, the top bit flips.
And the clock jumps back to nineteen-oh-one.
Most modern systems moved to sixty-four-bit time, good for two hundred ninety-two billion years.
But old devices and forgotten code are still counting toward twenty thirty-eight.
